MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the 6th multiple of 4? (1 mark)
   A. 24
   B. 20
   C. 28
   D. 10

2. Round 918 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 930
   C. 920
   D. 910

3. What is the total value of the digit 6 in 8,064? (1 mark)
   A. 60
   B. 10
   C. 600
   D. 6

4. Which statement about 90 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is neither even nor odd
   B. It is even because it ends in 0
   C. It is odd because it has an even number of digits
   D. It is odd because it ends in 0

5. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 2,999 + 3,001? (1 mark)
   A. 0
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 1

6. A classroom has 13 rows of 12 desks. How many desks are there? (1 mark)
   A. 156 desks
   B. 146 desks
   C. 256 desks
   D. 136 desks

7. A book costs Ksh 45. How much do 24 books cost? (1 mark)
   A. 1,070 shillings
   B. 1,180 shillings
   C. 1,060 shillings
   D. 1,080 shillings

8. What is 85 ÷ 5? (1 mark)
   A. 27
   B. 18
   C. 17
   D. 16

9. 45 eggs are packed in trays that each hold 6 eggs. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 8
   C. 6
   D. 9

10. Which division fact belongs to the same family as 4 × 6 = 24? (1 mark)
   A. 24 ÷ 4 = 4
   B. 24 ÷ 24 = 4
   C. 6 ÷ 4 = 24
   D. 24 ÷ 4 = 6

11. 47 mangoes are shared equally among 6 children. How many mangoes are left over? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 6
   C. 1
   D. 7

12. Chebet writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 5/12
   B. 9/9
   C. 8/3
   D. 2 5/8

13. What is 3/5 of 25? (1 mark)
   A. 15
   B. 10
   C. 5
   D. 20

14. Beth writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 11/5
   B. 3 1/2
   C. 1/2
   D. 2/9

15. What is 5/6 of 18? (1 mark)
   A. 18
   B. 3
   C. 15
   D. 11

16. What is the total value of the digit 6 in 5.68? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 0.6
   C. 600
   D. 0.06

17. A hundred square has 60 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.6
   B. 0.06
   C. 6
   D. 60

18. In the expression 3m + 2o, what does the letter o stand for if m is a bag of mangoes and 2o is 2 bags of oranges? (1 mark)
   A. The number 2
   B. The total number of bags
   C. One bag of oranges
   D. Two bags of mangoes

19. Which expression shows "5 more than x"? (1 mark)
   A. x ÷ 5
   B. x − 5
   C. x + 5
   D. 5x

20. Wairimu had d shillings and spent 45 shillings. Which expression shows the money she has left? (1 mark)
   A. d − 45
   B. 45d
   C. 45 − d
   D. d + 45

21. A rectangle is 12 cm long and 7 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 19 cm
   B. 84 cm
   C. 38 cm
   D. 40 cm

22. A rectangle is 20 cm long and 6 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 120 cm
   B. 52 cm
   C. 26 cm
   D. 54 cm

23. A rectangle is made of 11 rows with 5 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 16 square units
   B. 66 square units
   C. 55 square units
   D. 32 square units

24. What does volume measure? (1 mark)
   A. The space a solid object takes up
   B. The flat surface a shape covers
   C. The distance round a shape
   D. The time an event takes

25. What is 5 L − 2 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 2 3/4 L
   B. 2 1/2 L
   C. 3 L
   D. 2 1/4 L

26. Two 1/4 kg masses balance (1 mark)
   A. 3/4 kg
   B. 1/2 kg
   C. 1 kg
   D. 1/4 kg

27. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 4 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 4. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 5:20
   B. 4:04
   C. 4:40
   D. 4:20

28. How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 2
   C. 0
   D. 4

29. The table shows the pets kept by 10 families: dog 3, cat 3, rabbit 2, hen 2. How many are NOT hen? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 9
   C. 8
   D. 12

30. Which of these is a good way to collect data on favourite games? (1 mark)
   A. Count the desks
   B. Ask each pupil which game they like best and record the answer
   C. Write only your own favourite
   D. Guess what they like

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 5,000, 4,750, 4,500, 4,250. (3 marks)

32. Using the vehicle data (5 matatus, 2 boda bodas, 2 buses, 1 lorry), which type was seen most and how many more matatus than buses were seen? (3 marks)

33. On a poultry farm each of 16 hens lays 21 eggs in one month. How many eggs are laid altogether? (3 marks)

34. Describe how to make a 1/2 kg mass from sand using a 1 kg mass and a beam balance. (4 marks)

35. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 5, 9, 13, 17, ... and state the rule. (3 marks)

36. Explain why the parts must be equal when we write a fraction such as 1/4. (2 marks)

37. A farmer had 6,500 seedlings and planted 2,875. How many were left? Estimate first by rounding to the nearest ten. (4 marks)

38. A cuboid has a volume of 60 blocks. One layer has 12 blocks. How many layers does it have? (2 marks)

39. A trip costs Ksh t for each pupil. Write an expression for the cost for 20 pupils and find the cost if t = 150. (3 marks)

40. Divide 450 by 100 and give the remainder. Explain what the remainder means. (4 marks)

41. Start at 1,500 and add 1,000 each time to write a pattern of five numbers. State the rule. (3 marks)

42. Complete the pattern 3, 6, 12, 24, ... with the next two numbers and state the rule. (3 marks)

43. Explain the difference between a factor and a multiple, using the number 6 as an example. (3 marks)

44. Bags of 5 kg are filled from a 50 kg sack of rice. Find the number of bags. (2 marks)

45. Add 1 1/4 L and 2 1/2 L. Show your working. (3 marks)

46. A learner says the volume of a cuboid 4 blocks long, 3 wide and 2 high is 9 blocks because 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. What mistake did the learner make and what is the correct volume? (3 marks)

47. A tanker fills 100 jerrycans of 20 litres each. How many litres is that? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 24
   Multiply 4 × 6 = 24. It is the 6th multiple of 4.

2. C — 920
   Look at the ones digit 8. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 918 rounds to 920.

3. A — 60
   The digit 6 is in the tens place, so its total value is 6 × 10 = 60.

4. B — It is even because it ends in 0
   Look at the ones digit. 0 is even, so 90 is even.

5. C — 3
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 2,999 + 3,001 needs 3 regroupings.

6. A — 156 desks
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 156 desks.

7. D — 1,080 shillings
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 1,080 shillings.

8. C — 17
   5 × 17 = 85, so 85 ÷ 5 = 17.

9. B — 8
   45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3. The 3 left-over eggs need one more tray, so 8 trays are needed.

10. D — 24 ÷ 4 = 6
   Division undoes multiplication. Since 4 × 6 = 24, we know 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

11. A — 5
   47 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 5. Each child gets 7 and 5 are left.

12. A — 5/12
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 5/12 is less than one whole.

13. A — 15
   25 ÷ 5 = 5 and 5 × 3 = 15. So 3/5 of 25 is 15.

14. A — 11/5
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 11/5 is one whole or more.

15. C — 15
   18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 3 × 5 = 15. So 5/6 of 18 is 15.

16. B — 0.6
   The digit 6 is in the tenths place, so its total value is 0.6.

17. A — 0.6
   60 out of 100 squares is 60/100 = 0.6.

18. C — One bag of oranges
   The letter o stands for one bag of oranges. The number 2 in front tells us how many bags.

19. C — x + 5
   The key words tell us the operation. "5 more than x" is written x + 5.

20. A — d − 45
   Spent means take away, so she has d − 45 left.

21. C — 38 cm
   Perimeter = 12 + 7 + 12 + 7 = 38 cm.

22. B — 52 cm
   Perimeter = 20 + 6 + 20 + 6 = 52 cm.

23. C — 55 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 11 × 5 = 55 square units.

24. A — The space a solid object takes up
   Volume is the amount of space that a solid fills.

25. B — 2 1/2 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 5 L − 2 1/2 L = 2 1/2 L.

26. B — 1/2 kg
   1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2.

27. D — 4:20
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 4 shows 4 × 5 = 20 minutes, so the time is 4:20.

28. B — 2
   It folds along the line joining the middles of the long sides and the line joining the middles of the short sides.

29. C — 8
   10 − 2 = 8.

30. B — Ask each pupil which game they like best and record the answer
   Asking and recording the answers gives real data.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4,000, 3,750, 3,500 (rule: subtract 250)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three numbers.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Matatus. 5 − 2 = 3 more matatus than buses.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for matatu, 1 mark for 5 − 2, 1 mark for 3.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 336 eggs
   Working / marking points: 21 × 6 = 126 (1 mark); 21 × 10 = 210 (1 mark); 126 + 210 = 336 (1 mark).

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Balance a bag of sand against the 1 kg mass. Share the sand equally into two bags, checking with the balance that they are level. Each bag is 1/2 kg.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for balancing sand with 1 kg, 1 mark for sharing into two bags, 1 mark for checking they balance, 1 mark for stating each is 1/2 kg.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rule: add 4. Next numbers: 21, 25, 29.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three correct numbers (1 mark if only two are correct).

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. If the parts are different in size, one part is not one quarter of the whole.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying parts must be equal in size and 1 mark for the reason.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate 6,500 − 2,880 = 3,620. Exact: 3,625 seedlings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding 2,875 to 2,880 (6,500 stays), 1 mark for the estimate, 1 mark for the exact working, 1 mark for the answer.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: 5 layers
   Working / marking points: 60 ÷ 12 = 5. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20t. When t = 150, cost = 20 × 150 = Ksh 3,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 20t, 1 mark for replacing t by 150, 1 mark for Ksh 3,000.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4 remainder 50. There are 4 whole hundreds in 450 and 50 is left over.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4, 1 mark for remainder 50, 2 marks for the explanation.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,500, 2,500, 3,500, 4,500, 5,500. Rule: add 1,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for five correct terms (1 mark for three or four).

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rule: multiply by 2. Next numbers: 48 and 96.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule, 1 mark for each correct number.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: A factor divides a number exactly: the factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6. A multiple is found by multiplying: the multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning and 1 mark for correct examples.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: 10 bags
   Working / marking points: 50 ÷ 5 = 10. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Wholes 1 + 2 = 3 (1 mark); parts 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4 (1 mark); total 3 3/4 L (1 mark).

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: The learner added. She should multiply: one layer has 4 × 3 = 12 blocks and 2 layers make 24 blocks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mistake, 1 mark for the method, 1 mark for 24 blocks.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2,000 litres
   Working / marking points: 20 × 100 = 2,000. 1 mark for the multiplication and 1 mark for units.
